name: Data preparation
characteristic: what the procedure does to the example set
positive_test: acts on the training examples before they reach the learner
negative_test: acts on parameters, gradients or outputs
examples: tokenization, augmentation, curriculum

name: Input representation construction
positive_test: converts raw input into the units or features the model consumes
negative_test: changes which examples are present
examples: BPE, WordPiece, feature scaling, discretisation, spectrogram extraction, one-hot encoding

name: Example transformation
positive_test: emits a transformed version of an existing example for training
negative_test: emits an entirely new example
examples: mixup, CutMix, RandAugment, SpecAugment, back-translation, adversarial perturbation

name: Example selection, weighting and ordering
positive_test: decides which examples are used, with what weight, in what order
negative_test: changes the content of an example
examples: dedup, quality filtering, DoReMi, curriculum learning, active learning, class-imbalance resampling

name: Target construction for unlabelled data
positive_test: assigns a target to an example that did not have one
negative_test: assigns targets by a human annotator inside the run
examples: pseudo-labelling, Snorkel, label propagation, Dawid-Skene, HER relabelling

name: Example synthesis
positive_test: creates training examples that did not exist before
negative_test: transforms examples that already exist
examples: Self-Instruct, domain randomisation, generative oversampling, dataset distillation

name: Experience generation
characteristic: what determines the distribution of collected interaction
positive_test: determines what interaction data the learner sees, by acting
negative_test: consumes a fixed dataset
examples: epsilon-greedy, PER, self-play
notes: empty for any run with a static dataset

name: Behaviour and exploration policy
positive_test: decides which action is taken for data-collection purposes
negative_test: decides how the collected data updates parameters
examples: epsilon-greedy, Boltzmann exploration, UCB, Thompson sampling, RND bonus, NoisyNets

name: Experience storage and reuse
positive_test: decides which past interaction is replayed and with what target
negative_test: decides which fresh action to take
examples: experience replay, PER, HER, episodic memory, rehearsal buffers

name: Task and opponent generation
positive_test: decides which environment, goal or opponent the agent faces next
negative_test: decides the action within a fixed task
examples: self-play, PSRO, league training, PLR, POET, automatic domain randomisation

name: Producing or adapting the learned object
characteristic: which part of the fitting loop the procedure defines
positive_test: participates in turning data into parameters
negative_test: acts before data reaches the learner, or after parameters are final
examples: loss functions, optimisers, LoRA

name: Initialisation
positive_test: sets parameter values before any update
negative_test: changes parameters after updates have begun
examples: He init, Xavier init, orthogonal init, LSUV, Fixup, muP init

name: Objective definition
positive_test: defines the scalar the run minimises, including added penalty terms
negative_test: defines how that scalar's gradient is turned into a step
examples: cross-entropy, InfoNCE, ELBO, PPO surrogate, weight decay, KD loss, SAM
notes: the most crowded slot in the dimension

name: Estimator and inference engine
positive_test: defines how an intractable expectation or posterior is estimated or sampled
negative_test: defines the scalar being estimated
examples: REINFORCE estimator, reparameterisation trick, straight-through estimator, Gumbel-softmax, EM E-step, MCMC, variational inference, SMC
notes: the slot that makes classical statistics fit

name: Gradient post-processing
positive_test: modifies the gradient between the backward pass and the update
negative_test: modifies the loss, or the optimiser's internal state rule
examples: gradient clipping, gradient accumulation, PCGrad, DP-SGD noise, gradient compression at the worker

name: Parameter update rule
positive_test: maps a gradient and optimiser state to a parameter change
negative_test: produces the gradient, or decides which parameters are eligible
examples: SGD, momentum, Adam, AdamW, L-BFGS, Shampoo, Muon, CMA-ES, closed-form normal equations
notes: Adam never fills any other slot; the slot test passes cleanly

name: Optimisation schedule and control
positive_test: changes a hyperparameter of the update over the course of training
negative_test: changes the direction of the update
examples: cosine annealing, SGDR, warmup, one-cycle, ReduceLROnPlateau, batch-size ramps, EMA decay schedule

name: Adaptation scope
positive_test: decides which parameters are eligible to change, or adds new ones to change instead
negative_test: decides how eligible parameters change
examples: LoRA, adapters, prefix tuning, BitFit, linear probing, layer freezing, PackNet masks

name: Stopping and checkpoint selection
positive_test: decides when fitting ends or which produced checkpoint is kept
negative_test: decides the step size while fitting continues
examples: early stopping, patience, best-on-validation checkpointing, trial early-stopping in Hyperband

name: Execution strategy
characteristic: the physical resource across which the computation is laid out
positive_test: determines how a single logical run is physically carried out -- across workers, devices, or one device's memory hierarchy
negative_test: anything that changes what is computed rather than how it is carried out; a library that merely implements such a strategy
examples: all-reduce SGD, ZeRO, FedAvg
notes: renamed from R.coord after phase 1: `coordination across workers` left single-device procedures (FlashAttention, gradient checkpointing) with no slot on any axis

name: Replicated data-parallel execution
positive_test: every worker holds the full model and processes a different data shard
negative_test: workers hold different parts of the model
examples: synchronous SGD, ring all-reduce, Hogwild!, local SGD, DiLoCo, gossip SGD

name: Model-state partitioning
positive_test: the model's parameters, optimiser state or layers are split across devices
negative_test: the model is replicated
examples: ZeRO-1/2/3, FSDP, Megatron tensor parallel, GPipe, 1F1B, expert parallelism, ring attention

name: Communication reduction
positive_test: changes what or how often workers transmit, not what they compute locally
negative_test: changes which worker computes what
examples: gradient quantization, PowerSGD, top-k sparsification, infrequent averaging, hierarchical all-reduce

name: Memory-compute trade-off
positive_test: trades recomputation or data movement against stored state on one device
negative_test: trades work across devices
examples: gradient checkpointing, activation offload, CPU/NVMe offload, mixed precision with loss scaling

name: Constrained aggregation of client updates
positive_test: combines updates from parties that do not share raw data, under a stated constraint
negative_test: combines gradients from workers that share one dataset
examples: FedAvg aggregation, SCAFFOLD control variates, secure aggregation, trimmed-mean robust aggregation

name: Configuration search
characteristic: which part of the configuration is searched
positive_test: runs or simulates multiple configurations and selects among them by a measured signal
negative_test: fixes the configuration in advance
examples: random search, Hyperband, DARTS
notes: the inner trials are themselves runs

name: Hyperparameter search
positive_test: searches scalar or categorical settings of a fixed learning procedure
negative_test: searches the model's structure
examples: grid search, random search, TPE, SMAC, Hyperband, ASHA, PBT, muTransfer

name: Architecture search
positive_test: searches the structure of the model itself
negative_test: searches the optimiser's settings
examples: NASNet, ENAS, DARTS, Once-for-All, regularised evolution, zero-cost proxies

name: Pipeline and algorithm selection
positive_test: searches jointly over preprocessing, model family and their hyperparameters
negative_test: searches within one fixed model family
examples: Auto-WEKA, auto-sklearn, TPOT, AutoGluon

name: Procedure-policy search
positive_test: searches over which data or training procedure to apply, rather than model settings
negative_test: searches over the model or its scalars
examples: AutoAugment, Population-Based Augmentation, learned curricula, data-mixture search

name: Parameter-space rewriting
characteristic: what is changed about the stored parameters
positive_test: transforms an existing parameter set without redefining what the model computes
negative_test: fits parameters from data in the first place
examples: magnitude pruning, GPTQ, model soups

name: Sparsification
positive_test: removes parameters or structures from the computation
negative_test: changes the numeric representation of retained parameters
examples: magnitude pruning, lottery ticket, movement pruning, SparseGPT, Wanda, channel and head pruning

name: Precision reduction
positive_test: lowers the numeric precision of weights, activations or caches
negative_test: removes parameters
examples: GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, LLM.int8, QAT, LSQ, BinaryConnect, KV-cache quantization
notes: QAT also occupies R.fit.est via the straight-through estimator

name: Factorisation
positive_test: replaces a weight tensor with a product of smaller factors
negative_test: zeroes or requantises the original tensor
examples: SVD compression, Tucker and CP decomposition, ASVD

name: Parameter combination
positive_test: produces one parameter set by combining several
negative_test: produces one by combining several models' predictions
examples: model soups, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE, Fisher merging, SWA, EMA of weights

name: Producing outputs from the learned object
characteristic: what the procedure contributes between a trained model and an emitted result
positive_test: runs at inference and changes what is emitted, how it is scored, or what it was given
negative_test: changes the parameters
examples: beam search, RAG, conformal prediction

name: Output generation
positive_test: converts model scores into the emitted output
negative_test: explores multiple complete candidate outputs
examples: greedy, beam search, top-p, contrastive decoding, constrained decoding, speculative decoding, diffusion samplers, classifier-free guidance

name: Test-time search and deliberation
positive_test: spends extra inference compute exploring several reasoning or action paths
negative_test: emits one pass through the model
examples: self-consistency, best-of-n, tree of thoughts, ReAct, Reflexion, MCTS, MPC/CEM, A-star
notes: the cost shows up in the run's budget

name: Retrieval and context construction
positive_test: selects external content to place in the model's input at inference
negative_test: selects training examples before fitting
examples: BM25, DPR, HNSW index lookup, RAG, FiD, reranking, kNN-LM

name: Calibration, uncertainty and abstention
positive_test: converts outputs into calibrated probabilities, intervals or an abstention decision
negative_test: converts them into a different emitted answer
examples: temperature scaling, isotonic regression, conformal prediction, deep ensembles, MC dropout, OOD scoring

name: Inference-time aggregation
positive_test: combines outputs of several models or several samples into one
negative_test: combines their parameters
examples: voting, prediction averaging, stacking, MBR, Bayesian model averaging, MoE inference routing

name: Prediction rule
positive_test: computes the output by an explicit named procedure over stored data or fitted structure, with no model forward pass to delegate to
negative_test: emitting the forward pass of a separable model
examples: k-NN majority vote, kernel density prediction, LOESS local fit, Viterbi decoding of a CRF, GP posterior mean
notes: added after the k-NN worked example found no fitting slot

name: Explanation production
positive_test: produces a statement about the model's behaviour as the run's output
negative_test: produces a prediction about the data
examples: Grad-CAM, integrated gradients, LIME, SHAP, activation patching, sparse autoencoder features, CKA
notes: admitted because an explanation is an output

name: Test-time adaptation
characteristic: what is updated using test-time data
positive_test: updates the model or its statistics after deployment, using unlabelled test inputs
negative_test: updates using labelled target data before deployment
examples: TENT, TTT, SHOT, BN-statistic adaptation, CoTTA, test-time prompt tuning
notes: overlaps R.fit by construction; kept separate because "when" is definitional here

name: Evaluation and model assessment
positive_test: computes a reported performance or inference claim about the fitted object
negative_test: contributes to producing the object or its outputs
examples: k-fold cross-validation, bootstrap CIs, permutation tests, FDR control, LLM-as-judge scoring, significance tests
notes: the participant rule as written excludes this; see Tensions

name: Operator-level computation strategy
positive_test: reorganises how a single operator is computed on one device -- tiling, fusion, recomputation, memory-hierarchy placement
negative_test: a different operator (linear attention changes the function and is model-side); a package that ships such a kernel
examples: FlashAttention, FlashAttention-2, PagedAttention, fused optimiser kernels
notes: the boundary case both phase-1 runs named and neither could place
